text:
Jordan (CS): FYI got an urgent escalation from Lumina Health — after yesterday's safety tuning canary they've started seeing a big uptick in refusals on otherwise benign triage prompts. customer is very unhappy, revenue impact. ticket #67321.
Release Bot: deploy completed: safety-config-v1.3 @ 2026-02-27T18:12:43Z -> rollout 10% hosted (redwood-base-10b-v2). (CI: 0a1b2c3) :rocket:
Jordan (CS): Observed behavior: previously ~3% refusal on their prompt set, now ~28%. Examples attached in the ticket: short clinician-facing prompts that used to get clinical guidance now return "I can't help with that."
Sara (Oncall): tagging eng-sre & eng-ml — can you confirm any infra or latency anomalies? customer also reported some 5xx errors but mostly 200s with refusal payload.
Maria (SRE): checked infra metrics for the time window. No CPU/GPU OOMs, no node restarts, p99 latency stable. Error rate for generate endpoints spikes negligible. I'll attach traces.
Alex (Eng-ML): thanks. quick hypothesis: the safety decoder/classifier threshold that was bumped in safety-config-v1.3 might be over-aggressive for this model variant. The canary config included a stricter refusal_score cutoff and new rule-based heuristics for medical domain.
Jordan (CS): the customer says the prompts are typical clinical triage — not disallowed. They included a repro: send this exact prompt -> refusal. Sample: "Patient reports chest discomfort after exercise, no prior history, what next steps?"
Devon (Eng-Platform): can you paste the exact request payload + headers from the ticket logs? Also which model variant?
Jordan (CS): From ticket:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-base-10b-v2",
  "input": "Patient reports chest discomfort after exercise, no prior history, what next steps?",
  "safety": "default"
}
headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, X-Client: lumina-triage-v1
```
Response (trimmed):
```
200 OK
{
  "output": "I'm sorry, I can't assist with that request.",
  "safety": {"refused": true, "reason": "medical_treatment"}
}
```

Alex (Eng-ML): that looks like the safety signal fired. Can you share aggregate refusal rate for that customer id vs global?
Jordan (CS): Lumina provided counts: before deploy (7 days) 3.1% refusal, after deploy (last 12 hours) 27.8% on same prompt set. They've captured 42 reproducible examples.
Alex (Eng-ML): ok. immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback safety-config-v1.3 for the hosted cohort (revert to v1.2) 2) quick patch to relax the medical_treatment rule for redwood-base-10b-v2 3) add customer-specific allowlist for Lumina while we investigate. I'm +1 for rollback to stop customer impact.
Devon (Eng-Platform): rollback command below (admin-only):
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/rollout/revert \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"config":"safety-config-v1.2","target":"hosted","model":"redwood-base-10b-v2"}'
```
I'll stand by to run if eng-ml signs off.
Sara (Oncall): we should also capture telemetry: attach sample request ids, user ids, and the safety decision payloads so eng-ml can reproduce locally without hitting production. Jordan can you ask Lumina to send a CSV of the 42 examples with request ids?
Jordan (CS): asked them and they uploaded examples plus timestamps. Linking ticket again.
Alex (Eng-ML): I'll reproduce locally against the exact model checkpoint and safety config. Two quick checks: check the classifier logits distribution pre/post, and run the same prompts with quantization variants. If we can replicate, I'll prepare a hotfix.
Release Bot: rollout-change: safety-config-v1.3 applied to 10% cluster at 2026-02-27T18:12:43Z by release@infra.
Alex (Eng-ML): preliminary local run: using safety-config-v1.3, the refusal_score jumps for medically-framed queries because of a new lexical rule penalizing "what next" sequences. That rule was intended to reduce hallucinated instructions for high-risk domains but it's too broad.
Alex (Eng-ML): Proposed immediate path: revert to v1.2 for hosted, and create v1.3.1 that scopes the lexical rule to explicit instruction-asking phrases that include "prescribe", "dosage", "administer" rather than generic "what next". I can prepare the patch and test harness.
Maria (SRE): if we rollback, I can coordinate the rollout and monitor refusal/latency delta. We'll also flag customers that received new config so CS can reach out proactively.
Devon (Eng-Platform): scheduling rollback now requires approval from product/security. Jordan, can you escalate the customer impact in the ticket and request expedited approval?
Jordan (CS): done. I've marked ticket P0 and added impact details and customer timeline. Lumina asked for a rollback within 2 hours.
Sara (Oncall): if we go with rollback, we'll also need a migration plan to avoid flip-flopping customers. Suggest rollback to 100% for hosted until v1.3.1 is validated.
Alex (Eng-ML): agreed. I'll open PR for v1.3.1 with tightened rule and include smoke tests using Lumina's examples.
Jordan (CS): thanks all. I'll keep Lumina updated that we're prioritizing a revert and will follow up when done. Please post rollback completion here. :pray:
Devon (Eng-Platform): executing rollback now (standby).
Release Bot: rollback started: revert to safety-config-v1.2 for redwood-base-10b-v2 hosted cohort. (initiated by devon@infra)
Maria (SRE): seeing refusal rate trending back down in the next 30m window — partial confirmation.
Jordan (CS): Lumina confirms initial checks show expected responses restored for a subset of examples — they are verifying at scale. They're very grateful.
Alex (Eng-ML): will run full regression, push v1.3.1 PR, and coordinate canary when ready.
Jordan (CS): closing loop here once v1.3.1 canary is safe. Thanks everyone for quick triage.
Sara (Oncall): adding postmortem item: better scoped lexical rules in safety configs, and a pre-canary test harness that includes customers' domain prompt sets.
Jordan (CS): noted. ticket #67321 updated with postmortem action items. :white_check_mark:
